Figure 1:G-CAST, a governed continual adaptation loop for deployed e-commerce agents.
The main self-evolution loop converts daily production queries into checkpoint updates through multi-rollout generation, reward reliability checking, reward-routed data orchestration, model adaptation, and governed checkpoint transition. When rollout evidence indicates a possible reward error under the current contract, the reward-evolution loop updates the executable reward through contract-grounded annotation, offline reward checks, and trial adaptation before training resumes. Candidate checkpoints are admitted only after cumulative evaluation on both newly introduced and previously retained capabilities, with rejected candidates, regressions, and reward anomalies recorded in the evaluation ledger.

Figure 2:Performance degradation of a fixed checkpoint as the capability contract expands across demand periods.
The figure reports the base reward, which excludes auxiliary reward components introduced only in later contract versions, so that performance remains directly comparable across periods. The dark curve shows the cumulative mean over all active evaluation slices, and the colored curves show the period-specific means.
